That is 22 of the 36 and it is read off the figure, which is the only place the restriction appears: the datasheet says only '36 x 40/100/200/400G QSFP-DD service ports with 400G ZR/ZR+ support' without naming which" data-op2-option-ports="when the premium OP2 external TCAM is enabled, four service ports are taken for statistics and stop forwarding, leaving 32 - HIG Figure 10b/8b highlights them in yellow as ports 01, 17, 19 and 35" data-timing="Stratum 3E OCXO; SyncE; IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2); SMPTE ST 2059-2 (extra licence); T-BC/OC, T-TC" data-segment-routing="full SRv6" data-macsec="point-to-point MACsec" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 and micro-USB, both labelled IOIO, 115200 8N1 (micro-USB needs the Silicon Labs CP210x driver)" data-oob="1x 100M/1G RJ45 out-of-band management port" data-usb="1x USB 3.0 Type-A maintenance port" data-timing-inputs="1x 1PPS in/out SMB and 1x 10MHz in/out SMB, both premium-build only, 50 ohm, cable no longer than 3 m" data-safety="UL 62368-1, IEC 60950-1, IEC 62368-1, BSMI, MTCTE" data-emc="FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55032 Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32 Class A; MTCTE; Anatel" data-environment="RoHS, WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */

    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

That is 22 of the 36 and it is read off the figure, which is the only place the restriction appears: the datasheet says only '36 x 40/100/200/400G QSFP-DD service ports with 400G ZR/ZR+ support' without naming which" data-op2-option-ports="when the premium OP2 external TCAM is enabled, four service ports are taken for statistics and stop forwarding, leaving 32 - HIG Figure 10b/8b highlights them in yellow as ports 01, 17, 19 and 35" data-timing="Stratum 3E OCXO; SyncE; IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2); SMPTE ST 2059-2 (extra licence); T-BC/OC, T-TC" data-segment-routing="full SRv6" data-macsec="point-to-point MACsec" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 and micro-USB, both labelled IOIO, 115200 8N1 (micro-USB needs the Silicon Labs CP210x driver)" data-oob="1x 100M/1G RJ45 out-of-band management port" data-usb="1x USB 3.0 Type-A maintenance port" data-timing-inputs="1x 1PPS in/out SMB and 1x 10MHz in/out SMB, both premium-build only, 50 ohm, cable no longer than 3 m" data-safety="UL 62368-1, IEC 60950-1, IEC 62368-1, BSMI, MTCTE" data-emc="FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55032 Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32 Class A; MTCTE; Anatel" data-environment="RoHS, WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

That is 22 of the 36 and it is read off the figure, which is the only place the restriction appears: the datasheet says only '36 x 40/100/200/400G QSFP-DD service ports with 400G ZR/ZR+ support' without naming which" data-op2-option-ports="when the premium OP2 external TCAM is enabled, four service ports are taken for statistics and stop forwarding, leaving 32 - HIG Figure 10b/8b highlights them in yellow as ports 01, 17, 19 and 35" data-timing="Stratum 3E OCXO; SyncE; IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2); SMPTE ST 2059-2 (extra licence); T-BC/OC, T-TC" data-segment-routing="full SRv6" data-macsec="point-to-point MACsec" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 and micro-USB, both labelled IOIO, 115200 8N1 (micro-USB needs the Silicon Labs CP210x driver)" data-oob="1x 100M/1G RJ45 out-of-band management port" data-usb="1x USB 3.0 Type-A maintenance port" data-timing-inputs="1x 1PPS in/out SMB and 1x 10MHz in/out SMB, both premium-build only, 50 ohm, cable no longer than 3 m" data-safety="UL 62368-1, IEC 60950-1, IEC 62368-1, BSMI, MTCTE" data-emc="FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55032 Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32 Class A; MTCTE; Anatel" data-environment="RoHS, WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='ufispace/fan-808012@'] .state-fault { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/fan-808012@'] .state-ok { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-302-ac@'] .state-fault { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-302-ac@'] .state-in-range { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-302-ac@'] .state-ok { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-302-ac@'] .state-over-temp { --led-color: #f59e0b; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-302-ac@'] .state-over-temp { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-302-ac@'] .state-standby { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-302-ac@'] .state-standby { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
</style>

That is 22 of the 36 and it is read off the figure, which is the only place the restriction appears: the datasheet says only '36 x 40/100/200/400G QSFP-DD service ports with 400G ZR/ZR+ support' without naming which" data-op2-option-ports="when the premium OP2 external TCAM is enabled, four service ports are taken for statistics and stop forwarding, leaving 32 - HIG Figure 10b/8b highlights them in yellow as ports 01, 17, 19 and 35" data-timing="Stratum 3E OCXO; SyncE; IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2); SMPTE ST 2059-2 (extra licence); T-BC/OC, T-TC" data-segment-routing="full SRv6" data-macsec="point-to-point MACsec" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 and micro-USB, both labelled IOIO, 115200 8N1 (micro-USB needs the Silicon Labs CP210x driver)" data-oob="1x 100M/1G RJ45 out-of-band management port" data-usb="1x USB 3.0 Type-A maintenance port" data-timing-inputs="1x 1PPS in/out SMB and 1x 10MHz in/out SMB, both premium-build only, 50 ohm, cable no longer than 3 m" data-safety="UL 62368-1, IEC 60950-1, IEC 62368-1, BSMI, MTCTE" data-emc="FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55032 Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32 Class A; MTCTE; Anatel" data-environment="RoHS, WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

That is 22 of the 36 and it is read off the figure, which is the only place the restriction appears: the datasheet says only '36 x 40/100/200/400G QSFP-DD service ports with 400G ZR/ZR+ support' without naming which" data-op2-option-ports="when the premium OP2 external TCAM is enabled, four service ports are taken for statistics and stop forwarding, leaving 32 - HIG Figure 10b/8b highlights them in yellow as ports 01, 17, 19 and 35" data-timing="Stratum 3E OCXO; SyncE; IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2); SMPTE ST 2059-2 (extra licence); T-BC/OC, T-TC" data-segment-routing="full SRv6" data-macsec="point-to-point MACsec" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 and micro-USB, both labelled IOIO, 115200 8N1 (micro-USB needs the Silicon Labs CP210x driver)" data-oob="1x 100M/1G RJ45 out-of-band management port" data-usb="1x USB 3.0 Type-A maintenance port" data-timing-inputs="1x 1PPS in/out SMB and 1x 10MHz in/out SMB, both premium-build only, 50 ohm, cable no longer than 3 m" data-safety="UL 62368-1, IEC 60950-1, IEC 62368-1, BSMI, MTCTE" data-emc="FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55032 Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32 Class A; MTCTE; Anatel" data-environment="RoHS, WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>
